_comment: Which names a body declares, forced through both runtimes so the Kotlin twin cannot drift. `names` is null when the body does not parse. Whitespace is an explicit class in both, never a shorthand: the two disagree about which characters count.

cases.name: each name once, in the order the body first mentions it
whitespace inside the braces is not part of the name
a body with nothing to fill declares nothing
a single brace pair opens no placeholder
prose closing nested JSON is literal
an underscore and digits are part of a name after the first letter
a newline inside the braces still names the parameter
a tab inside the braces still names the parameter
an opener that names nothing refuses the whole body
a nested opener refuses, since one of them closes nothing
a name may not start with a digit
empty braces name nothing
a hyphen is not part of a name, so the placeholder never closes
a placeholder at each end of the body is found
an empty body declares nothing
the scan carries on past a good placeholder to refuse a later opener
two placeholders touching, the second of them malformed
a non-breaking space opens nothing, since the runtimes disagree about calling it whitespace
a placeholder found after a long literal run
a repeated opener before a good one refuses rather than skipping to it
